seed.description: The same intent and seed always compose the same map.

settings.description: Stamp tags the map is made from: only stamps carrying at least one are used (e.g. a setting and "generic" pieces); none: any stamp.

ground.description: The ground under everything; null for none (an interior on a bare scene).

lighting.description: Day leaves the scene lit. Dim (an interior, the underhive) is half dark, each room lit by its own light and its lamps, the walls cutting the light. By night the scene is dark and rooms are lit by what is in them (a hearth, lamps), not a flat light; a room with nothing to light it keeps its own.

groundTexture.description: A texture role of the active set to draw the ground in (`floor.scorched-earth`); null for its biome’s own. A role the set lacks draws as the biome.

backdrop.description: The colour shown round the map where nothing is drawn (the void round a ship, the dark round a tunnel), `#rrggbb`; null: the scene’s own.

key.description: A name roads and rivers can start or end at.

depth.description: How far in from the edge.

centre.description: In grid squares from the map’s top-left corner.

items.description: In grid squares from the map’s top-left corner.

texture.description: A texture role of the active set to draw the ground in (`floor.scorched-earth`); null for its biome’s own. A role the set lacks draws as the biome.

soft.description: Paving only: its edge feathered rather than crisp (standing water, a stain), not laid hard standing.

anyOf.description: In grid squares from the map’s top-left corner.

from.description: Where a road or river starts or ends: a map edge (a point along it), a point, a building (its entrance), or a zone by key (its edge nearest the other end: a river running out of a lake).

anyOf.description: In grid squares from the map’s top-left corner.

to.description: Where a road or river starts or ends: a map edge (a point along it), a point, a building (its entrance), or a zone by key (its edge nearest the other end: a river running out of a lake).

width.description: Squares across; omitted: a road 1.5, a river 2.

meander.description: How much it winds: 0 straight, 1 a lot.

key.description: A name roads can run to.

at.description: Top-left corner. Omitted: centred on the map.

floor.description: Floor texture role (a biome or a pack floor.*).

wall.description: Wall texture role (a pack wall.*), drawn along every wall.

wallBand.description: A band this many squares deep of its wall material round the outside of its footprint, broken at its doorways: heavy masonry. Null: its walls alone.

entrance.description: The side its front door faces.

frontDoor.description: Has a front door; false: no way in through its outer walls but its `openings` (a guest floor reached only by its stair, a sealed vault).

frontDoorAt.description: Squares along the entrance side from its top or left end where the front door stands; null: anywhere along the entrance room’s outer wall.

frontDoorOpen.description: The front door standing open (stuck on seized hinges, left unbarred).

frontDoorGap.description: No door at all where the front door would be: a breach, a street running on off the map.

doorAnimation.description: How its doors open, where no door art hangs in the doorway: `slide` (a panel into the wall, seen open as a bare doorway), `ascend` (a shutter rising), `swing` on hinges; null: Foundry’s default swing.

doorTags.description: Door art its doorways are hung with must carry one of these tags (`timber`, `bulkhead`, `blast`); none: any door art as wide as the doorway.

key.description: This room’s name among the building’s rooms, for `opensTo`.

size.description: Floor area relative to the building’s other rooms (2 is twice as big as 1).

opensTo.description: Rooms it has a door into; the layout puts them side by side.

doorOpen.description: Its doors to the rooms it opens onto stand open (a room left open, its sliding door slid back).

archTo.description: Rooms it opens onto through a doorless archway: the wall they share open but for a pier at each end (a corridor’s mouth), or only `archWidth` of it.

archWidth.description: Squares across its archways, the rest of each shared wall left standing (a narthex walled off from its nave but for one arch in line with the aisle); null: the whole wall but its piers.

archAt.description: Where along each shared wall the centre of an `archWidth` archway stands, as a fraction of that wall from its top or left end; null: its middle.

secretTo.description: Rooms it opens onto through a secret door: plain wall to look at from either side, a native secret door to find (a vault behind a crypt).

doorAt.description: Where along each wall it shares a door through stands, as a fraction of that wall from its top or left end (a row of identical cells); null: anywhere.

entrance.description: Has the building’s front door. Without one marked, the first room has it.

floor.description: Its own floor texture role (a kitchen’s flagstones among plank rooms); omitted, the building’s.

rect.description: Exactly where it lies, in squares from the building’s top-left corner. When every room of a floor gives one, the layout is taken as given.

grime.description: How much grime (stains, cracks, dust) gathers on its floor along its walls: 0 none, 1 filthy; a little when omitted.

chamfer.description: Its corners cut off diagonally this many squares (an octagonal chamber), the cut corners solid masonry; null: square corners.

chamferAt.description: Which corners its chamfer cuts: all four (an octagonal chamber), or some (a hull tapering to its bow, a blunt stern).

fixtures.description: Named pieces it holds, placed first, each where asked.

name.description: What it is, written on its placeholder box where no stamp draws it (“filing cabinets”, “drain grate”).

role.description: The stamp role that draws it, where a pack has art for it; omitted, it is always a labelled box.

tags.description: Art of its role must carry one of these tags (a `reception` counter, not a food stall); none: any art of the role.

width.description: Its size in squares, its back along the width: its art is fitted to it, and it is the box it stands as where no stamp draws it.

reads.description: What players read on it by hovering over it: a sign's words, a plaque's inscription, a notice pinned to a board.

state.description: The state its art is drawn in, by the words of a variant's state (a locker `ajar`, a lamp `lit`): the first variant whose state holds them; else as drawn.

facing.description: Which way its front faces, standing free (centre, a point, a grid).

fixed.description: Exactly where asked, whatever is there: hung overhead or laid flush (a sign over a door, a floor inlay), or meant to block the way (rubble spilling from a collapsed doorway, a rockfall choking a tunnel). It keeps no floor from other pieces.

open.description: Ends of its run (map sides) drawn without their end pieces, to butt square against another run: an L-shaped counter is two runs, one `open` where it meets the other. They must be the ends its `facing` gives it (left or right facing up or down; top or bottom facing sideways).

count.description: How many, against a wall, in corners or along a line; rows and grids set their own.

standoff.description: Squares out from the wall (a bar counter with the barkeep behind it).

anyOf.description: Against a wall, its back to it, facing into the room.
In a corner.
In the middle of the room.

astride.description: Centred on the point even where that sets it into the wall (a firing port in a hull), never drawn in to stand wholly inside the room; it stands there as a `fixed` piece does.

anyOf.description: At this point of the room, as fractions of its size.
`count` of them evenly along a line across the room, from one point to the other, as fractions of its size (stools before a bar).

area.description: Part of the room, from its top-left corner to its bottom-right, as fractions of the room’s size.

anyOf.description: Evenly spaced across the room (or its `area`), columns by rows (a nave’s column footprints, three vats in a row).

rows.description: Rows along the room’s long axis, or across it.

aisle.description: Squares of aisle between rows and at their ends.

max.description: Rows at most; omitted, as many as fit.

behind.description: At its back instead (the clerk’s chair behind a desk, where the visitor’s is before it).

place.description: Where the fixture stands in its room.

state.description: The state its art is drawn in, by the words of a variant's state (a locker `ajar`, a lamp `lit`): the first variant whose state holds them; else as drawn.

facing.description: Which way its front faces, standing free (centre, a point, a grid).

fixed.description: Exactly where asked, whatever is there: hung overhead or laid flush (a sign over a door, a floor inlay), or meant to block the way (rubble spilling from a collapsed doorway, a rockfall choking a tunnel). It keeps no floor from other pieces.

open.description: Ends of its run (map sides) drawn without their end pieces, to butt square against another run: an L-shaped counter is two runs, one `open` where it meets the other. They must be the ends its `facing` gives it (left or right facing up or down; top or bottom facing sideways).

at.description: Its centre, in grid squares from the map’s top-left corner.

items.description: A named piece standing outside (a flight of steps, a plinth, a drain grate), placed before anything is scattered.

stair.description: Its stair up from the ground; null for one reached from beyond the map (an overpass from wall to wall).

side.description: The side of the platform its stair climbs to.

at.description: Where along that side the stair arrives, in squares from its top or left end.

items.description: A raised platform: its floor on the level above the ground, railed round but where its stair from the ground arrives.
